source.title: Towards Load-Aware Prefill Deflection for Disaggregated LLM Serving
source.summary: Disaggregated LLM serving runs prefill and decode on separate GPU pools to keep the two phases from interfering. In practice, this creates a new asymmetry: under bursty, heavy-tailed workloads prefill nodes saturate while decode nodes have compute underutilized, and on a production-style A100 cluster with 2 prefill and 2 decode nodes (2P2D), we find that prefill execution accounts for only 2-23% of P95 Time-to-First-Token (TTFT). Queuing and inter-node GPU-GPU KV-cache transfer account for the rest. We present a proactive prefill-deflecting scheduler that lets decode nodes serve prefill phase of requests as chunked-prefill steps interleaved with their in-flight decode batches. For each queued request, we estimate the TTFT it would see on the prefill node, and on every decode node, search for the largest chunk schedule that keeps in-flight decodes within their Time-Between-Tokens (TBT) SLO and deflect when the decode path helps tail latency. Because the prefill phase of deflected requests runs in place on the decode node, the inter-node KV transfer is eliminated. Implemented on vLLM and evaluated on production-style traces with DeepSeek-V2-Lite, our approach reduces P95 TTFT by upto 81% and raises SLO attainment by upto 79% over state-of-the-art disaggregated schedulers, at sub-millisecond per-request routing cost.

previous_facts.title: Towards Load-Aware Prefill Deflection for Disaggregated LLM Serving
previous_facts.event_hint: Kairos: a proactive prefill-deflection scheduler for disaggregated LLM serving that reroutes prefill to underutilized decode nodes as chunked-prefill steps, eliminating inter-node KV transfer and cutting P95 TTFT up to 81%.
previous_facts.problem: In disaggregated LLM serving (separate prefill and decode GPU pools), bursty heavy-tailed workloads saturate prefill nodes while decode nodes sit underutilized. On a production-style 2P2D A100 cluster, prefill execution accounts for only 2-23% of P95 TTFT; the rest is prefill queueing and inter-node GPU-to-GPU KV-cache transfer.
previous_facts.mechanism: Kairos estimates, at scheduling time, the TTFT a queued request would see on the prefill node, and for every decode node sweeps candidate chunk-size sequences to find the largest schedule that keeps in-flight decodes within their Time-Between-Tokens (TBT) SLO, then deflects the prefill phase to a decode node when the decode path helps tail latency. Because the deflected prefill runs in place on the decode node, the inter-node KV transfer is eliminated. A single operator-tunable knob alpha >= 1 bounds TTFT regression for deflected requests.

evidence.claim: Prefill execution accounts for only 2-23% of P95 TTFT across five workloads; queue wait and inter-node KV-cache transfer account for the remaining 77-98%.
On the bursty workload, P95 TTFT was 7893.9 ms, with prefill queue 840.8 ms, prefill exec 1070.1 ms, KV transfer 2175.6 ms, decode queue 55.6 ms; KV transfer reached up to 4.2 s at P95 for LPLD.
Prefill SM utilization was 75-84% across workloads while decode SM utilization never exceeded 27%; the gap was widest for HPLD (84% vs 7.5%).
Kairos reduces P95 TTFT by up to 81% and raises SLO attainment by up to 79% over state-of-the-art disaggregated schedulers, at sub-millisecond per-request routing cost.
evidence.value: up to 81% P95 TTFT reduction; up to 79% SLO attainment gain

evidence.claim: Implemented on vLLM 0.18.1 in approximately 2000 lines of Python; per-request scheduling overhead is less than 1 ms; chunked-prefill step latency stayed flat (delta Tstep <= 30 ms) for chunk sizes up to 512 tokens across workloads and batch sizes.
evidence.value: <1 ms routing; ~2000 LoC; <=30 ms step-latency increase up to chunk size 512
evidence.source_locator: Contributions (PDF Page 2); Figure 1 caption, PDF Page 5

previous_facts.evaluation_context: Production-derived request traces replayed against DeepSeek-V2-Lite (MoE), token counts normalized to its 32K context window (prompt P25/median/P90 = 2071/3569/10366, median P:D ratio 69.7). Cluster: 2 prefill + 2 decode nodes (2P2D), each NVIDIA A100 80GB. Five workloads (LPLD, LPHD, HPLD, HPHD, Bursty). SLO targets: 4 s P95 TTFT, 70 ms TBT. Per-node utilization captured via NVIDIA Nsight Systems. Baselines include state-of-the-art disaggregated schedulers (Splitwise/DistServe/Mooncake/TetriInfer family).
previous_facts.limitations: Chunk sizes >= 1024 increase decode step latency (up to ~50 ms for bursty/high-prefill workloads) and require knowledge of cached-token volume, so chunk selection is regime-dependent. The headline 81%/79% gains are stated relative to state-of-the-art disaggregated schedulers but the precise baseline system identity and the detailed comparison table are not in the reviewed front evidence. 2P2D is the main configuration (footnote notes 1P3D saturates the single prefill node and 3P1D is decode-capacity-limited).
previous_facts.project_relevance: Directly relevant to KV-cache transfer and state-aware scheduling. It shows that under disaggregated serving, KV transfer and prefill queueing dominate tail TTFT, and that a load-aware scheduler aware of KV-cache occupancy, decode batch state, and per-step latency can eliminate inter-node KV transfer by deflecting prefill. This is a concrete case where network-side / cross-node coordination adds value beyond pure per-GPU memory scheduling.
source_notes: The 2-23% prefill-execution share and the full P95 TTFT breakdown (Table 3) are fully visible and verified.
Utilization figures (75-84% / <=27%) are from Table 2 (PDF Page 4).
The 81%/79% headline and <1 ms routing cost are restated identically in the Abstract and the Contributions list.
